text:
Assistant B is better. It gives a fuller, clearer explanation that suits a non-technical audience. It states that language models are mostly trained on unlabeled text, because so much of it is available, and that the model learns patterns between words. It also gives concrete examples of labels (sentiment, topic, intent) and explains when labeled data is useful.

Assistant A is correct but terse and somewhat jargon-heavy. It doesn't say which kind of data is typical, and it offers no examples.

Assistant B has minor flaws. Its phrase "can generate text that sounds like it was written by a human" is a loose gloss. The claim that labeled data is needed to train a language model for specific tasks is somewhat conflated with fine-tuning. Even so, it is more helpful and more accurate in emphasis.

[[B]]
